purpose: Exploratory discovery on the math subset, not held-out evaluation
scope: dataset == "math", 30180 of the 102014 train rows at the pinned revision
candidate_id_convention: <detector_id>:<lowest row_index in the candidate>, stable only at this revision
snapshot_provenance: Local copy verified against the pinned revision from the HuggingFace download metadata in .cache/huggingface/download (commit sha plus per-file sha256) before any row-indexed claim was recorded.
limits: Only the math subset was screened. The other subsets are unlabeled, not known good.
Only byte-identical prompts are compared, so every duplicate count is a lower bound; the corridor problem in ER-a3060c49 appears in two wordings differing by one comma and is counted as two groups.
Reference normalization is lenient by design. It is conservative for claiming a genuine conflict and permissive for claiming a notation variant, so both classes were read by hand before adjudication.

The 38 notation_variant_reference candidates were all read by hand; their decision between behavior_only and rejected then follows one mechanical rule, whether the copies also record different pass rates.

sentinel_reference, duplicate_prompt and unstable_passrate were adjudicated on named exemplars only. The remaining candidates in those classes are unreviewed and support the aggregate counts, not individual claims.
No rollouts were generated, no model was run, and the dataset's own verifier was never executed. Where a reference answer is called wrong, the answer was computed independently of the dataset.
Pass rates are read as published data. The dispersion test rejects the shared-policy independence null but cannot identify what replaced it.
Row indices are zero-based positions in the train split, counting shards in filename order, and are valid only at this revision.
